variant_id=BTK-p.Arg28His gene=BTK accession=Q06187 position=28 reference=R alternate=H

Task: HYPOTHESES. Read the shared record evidence (E1-E21, G1-G6). Note that knowledge_graph reports the graph is not yet consistent for E3, E6, E8, E10 and E12. Form competing agent-generated hypotheses for how R28H reduces BTK function. Candidates include loss of PIP3 or Ins(1,3,4,5)P4 binding, weakened phosphatidylserine-mediated membrane recruitment, altered PH-TH dimerization, and a shift in the closed-to-open equilibrium. For each hypothesis, state which one the starting evidence favours and what would refute it.

name: record_hypothesis
arguments: {"statement": "Arg28 in the BTK PH domain contacts the inositol-phosphate headgroup (Ins(1,3,4,5)P4, and plausibly PIP3). R28H removes the positive charge and weakens headgroup binding, so the PH domain docks less well to the membrane and BTK is recruited and activated less efficiently.", "mechanism_class": "ligand_binding", "supports": ["E7", "E3", "E2", "E1", "E11"], "would_refute": "Structures with Ins(1,3,4,5)P4 or PIP3-type headgroups bound to the BTK PH domain show no ligand atom within about 4 \u00c5 of residue 28, or docking/MM-PBSA of R28H against Ins(1,3,4,5)P4 gives a binding free energy change within noise of wild type (about 0.5 kcal/mol or less). The existing ligand-bound structures 6TT2 and 7I97 (ZN, MG, A1B6P) do not count as a test because they contain no inositol-phosphate ligand.", "starting_rank": 1, "rank_rationale": "This is the only hypothesis with a direct link to R28: UniProt annotates residue 28 as an Ins(1,3,4,5)P4 binding site (E7, experimental), and a computational MD/MM-PBSA study (E3) classed R28H as a functional, binding-altering mutant rather than a folding mutant. Pathogenic ClinVar and UniProt calls (E1, E2) and AlphaMissense (E11) fit a loss of function, but none of them names a mechanism. The rank is weak because E3 is a computational prediction and is flagged as not yet consistent in the knowledge graph, and no assay of R28H binding exists (G1, G2). The ligand-bound structures lack inositol phosphate, so they cannot test this hypothesis yet."}

name: record_hypothesis
arguments: {"statement": "R28 sits at or near the PH-TH module interface that drives BTK dimerization or oligomerization, and R28H weakens this contact. Reduced PH-TH dimerization then lowers the signalling output, or shifts the balance between the active and inactive oligomeric states.", "mechanism_class": "protein_interaction", "supports": ["E6", "E10", "E12", "E5"], "would_refute": "In PH-TH or full-length BTK dimer models and structures, residue 28 has no side-chain atom within about 4.5 \u00c5 of the partner chain, and the R28H \u0394\u0394G for dimer formation is near zero. A second refutation: a predicted dimer interface that does not include residue 28 and an R28H model that keeps the dimer contact intact.", "starting_rank": 2, "rank_rationale": "This hypothesis is supported only indirectly. E6 and E10 show that PH-TH dimerization and inositol-phosphate-dependent oligomerization are regulatory levers in this domain, but neither paper names R28 as an interface residue, and E6 is flagged as not yet consistent in the knowledge graph. E12 (closed/open equilibrium) is general and does not name R28. Without an interface structure or an R28-specific dimerization assay (G3), it ranks below the ligand-binding hypothesis. It is kept distinct from ligand binding because it predicts a loss of homo-oligomer contact rather than loss of headgroup contact."}

name: record_hypothesis
arguments: {"statement": "R28 packs into the PH-domain core or a buried \u03b2-strand (UniProt residues 25-32 are a \u03b2-strand, E9), and the Arg-to-His change strains the fold enough to lower its thermodynamic stability and folding yield, so less functional protein reaches the membrane.", "mechanism_class": "stability_folding", "supports": ["E9", "E13", "E14", "E18", "E15"], "would_refute": "R28 side-chain solvent accessibility is high across the 39 PDB structures that observe it (E15), and a stability predictor or FoldX-type calculation gives \u0394\u0394G below about 1 kcal/mol for R28H. Because E3 classed R28H as a functional rather than folding mutant, a folding-only mechanism would also be refuted by R28H-specific MD showing no local unfolding or RMSF change.", "starting_rank": 3, "rank_rationale": "Support for this hypothesis is generic: high conservation (E13, 0.962), a strongly deleterious popEVE score (E14), a \u03b2-strand annotation (E9), and high AlphaFold confidence (E18). None of these is specific to R28H. E3, the one study that examined R28H directly, explicitly classed it as a functional rather than folding mutant. It stays in the record as a rival class so the orchestrator can test it, but it ranks last."}
